canonical_title: Kalayavana Is Burned by Muchukunda's Glance
notes: Same event in HV 1.114 and BP 10.51: Krishna lures Kalayavana into the cave; the sleeping Muchukunda burns him with his gaze.
Same departure scene (VP 5.37, MB 16.4): the serpent Sesha issues from Balarama and enters the ocean.
Same feat (HV 1.102, BP 10.65): inebriated Balarama drags the Yamuna with his plough until the river begs pardon.
Same visit (HV 1.102, BP 10.65): Balarama returns to Nanda's village and the gopis.
Same catastrophe (VP 5.37, BP 11.30, MB 16.3): the kinsmen destroy one another with reed-weapons.

canonical_title: The Sages Curse Samba and the Yadavas
notes: Same curse episode (BP 11.1, MB 16.1): youths disguise Samba as a pregnant woman; the sages curse him to bear the iron bolt.
Same assembly scene (BP 10.74, MB 2.41): Shishupala derides Krishna's deeds and honour.
Same slaying (BP 10.74, MB 2.42): the discus ends Shishupala after the hundredth offence.

canonical_title: Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna Approach Jarasandha in Disguise
notes: Same journey (MB 2.20-21, BP 10.72): the three come to Girivraja as brahmanas asking alms.

canonical_title: Krishna Reveals Their Identities and Challenges Jarasandha
notes: Same confrontation (MB 2.22, BP 10.72): Krishna casts off the disguise; Jarasandha taunts; single combat is set.

canonical_title: Krishna Sports with His Sixteen Thousand Wives
notes: Same scene (HV 1.235, BP 10.90): Krishna's water-sports; each queen believes she alone is favoured.

canonical_title: Krishna Names the Pandavas to Balarama
notes: Same identification scene (MB 1.189, 1.191): at the svayamvara Krishna tells Balarama who each disguised brother is.

canonical_title: The Yadavas Resolve to Abandon Mathura for Dwaraka
notes: Same decision (HV ~1.113; one member carries a mis-cited locator "1.35" — content is the Kalayavana-era flight; confidence lowered for that locator).
Same founding (BP 10.50, HV 1.115): Krishna selects the sea-site; the divine architect raises the city.

canonical_title: Krishna, Balarama and Pradyumna Fly to Sonitpura on Garuda
notes: Round-2 audit merge: HV 1.264 (eight-armed divine form) and 1.268 (Garuda flight after Narada's report) are the same departure beat for the Bana-war rescue of Aniruddha.
